subject: Burst entitlement request for Acuity Health launch - throughput and monitoring plan

Subject: Traffic spike forecast + short-term throughput request for Apr 26 launch

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Attaching our launch forecast (acuity_traffic_forecast_Q2.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan. Topline: our marketing promo goes live Apr 26 18:00 PT and we expect a concentrated 45–90 minute surge from existing users and new signups.

Estimated peak: 1.2k–1.6k requests/sec to the Redwood text-generation endpoint for our chat flows, ~45k tokens/sec at peak. Baseline is ~80 RPS today.

Request: Can Redwood provision a temporary throughput entitlement (burst) to cover up to 1.8k RPS for a 2–3 hour window on Apr 26, with a canary 30-minute ramp before full blast? We need:
- confirmation of feasibility
- monitoring hooks and alert thresholds
- any required contract note or billing addendum

Attached: forecast PDF and a MAP spreadsheet (mutual-action-plan_AC-4721.xlsx).

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can finalize our rollout plan.

—Jason Miller
Senior Product Manager, Acuity Health

Jason — thanks for the detail and the attachments. Looping in Dev (serving/runtime), Laura (product + rollouts), Marissa (capacity ops) and Karthik (sales-engineering) to scope an internal plan.

Initial answers / asks from my side:
- We can support a short-lived burst entitlement but need to confirm exact RPS and token budget. Your forecast numbers are helpful; please confirm tokens per request (avg tokens per response + prompt).
- Proposed internal approach: canary (30m), staged ramp (30m), full window (90m) with automatic rollback if error-rate or latency breaches thresholds.
- Please confirm the preferred launch window in UTC as well.
- We will require a signed one-page addendum to the order for the burst credit/billing uplift.

Dev / Laura / Marissa / Karthik — can you review feasibility + approve guardrails? I suggest we aim for an internal runbook and a dedicated alert dashboard by Apr 22.

Grace O'Connor

Subject: Re: Traffic spike forecast + short-term throughput request for Apr 26 launch

Quick technical summary from infra/runtime:
- Current account quota (baseline): 150 RPS; soft autoscale allows short bursts but not to 1.8k without explicit entitlement.
- Feasible short-term approaches:
  1) Burst entitlement on hosted pool (fastest); we can carve 1.5k RPS for a 3-hour window if agreed — requires reservation of node capacity and temporary routing policy.
  2) Route traffic to a dedicated shard/pool (Dedicated capacity) — more isolation but needs provisioning lead time (~48–72h).
- Risk: increasing to >1k RPS without isolation may impact noisy-neighbor latency for other customers; we can mitigate with strict capacity reservation + KV cache priming.

Operational checklist I propose:
- Pre-warm KV caches and common prefixes 24h prior (we can run a priming script on Apr 25 18:00 PT).
- Canary window: 30m at 25% target (300–400 RPS), monitor p95 latency, error-rate, token throughput.
- Ramp phases: 30m increments to 50% then 100%.
- Alert thresholds to create: error_rate > 1% sustained 2m, p95 latency > 800ms, GPU memory > 85% on pool nodes.
- Telemetry: per-route token/sec, per-customer RPS, and headroom metric for serving queue.

Numbers I can commit to now: we can safely hit 1.5k RPS for a 3-hour window with the reservation approach; 1.8k is borderline without dedicated nodes. If Acuity confirms tokens per request (Jason), I’ll run a capacity check and request the node reservation.

Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Traffic spike forecast + short-term throughput request for Apr 26 launch

Thanks everyone — I reviewed the MAP and the infra notes. Product sign-off conditions below:

We will approve a temporary entitlement up to 1.5k RPS for a 3-hour window on Apr 26 with the following mandatory conditions:
- Canary + staged ramp as outlined by Dev; smoke test (5–10 test sessions) 60m before the canary.
- Marissa to reserve the capacity and flag the reservation in our console (ticket + booking ID).
- Jason / Acuity to sign a one-page addendum covering billing uplift and liability (Grace / Karthik to own).
- Real-time dashboard available to Acuity and Redwood: token/sec, p95 latency, error rate, and node headroom.

If any of the hard thresholds breach (error_rate > 1% sustained over 2m OR p95 latency > 800ms), automatic rollback to baseline will trigger and we will pause the marketing push.

I’ll update the MAP spreadsheet with these conditions and send the revised file.

Laura Bennett
